name: Paolo Ardoino
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Paolo Ardoino is CEO of crypto firm Tether.
Ardoino worked as a computer programmer before joining Tether's sister company, Bitfinex, as a senior software developer in 2014.
The biggest stablecoin issuer, Tether generated more than $10 billion in profit in 2025, largely from interest on the reserves backing USDT.
Ardoino owns an estimated 19% stake in the business.

name: Jude Reyes
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Together Jude Reyes and his brother Chris run Reyes Holdings, a $40 billion (sales) food and beverage distribution company.
The company got its start when the two brothers and their father bought a small Schlitz beer distributor in South Carolina for $740,000 in 1976.
Divisions include food distributor Martin-Brower, beer distributor Reyes Beverage Group and bottlers Great Lakes Coca-Cola and Reyes Holdings Coca Cola.
Younger brother Duke Reyes is CEO, while brothers James and Tom are executives at Reyes Beverage Group.
forbes_facts: Reyes Beverage Group distributes 171 million cases of beer each year.
Reyes Group arm Martin Brower delivers food to McDonald's, Panera and Chick-fil-A locations.

name: Gabe Newell
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Gabe Newell has led Valve Corp., which develops video games, since he cofounded it in 1998 with former Microsoft colleague Mike Harrington.
The company found initial success with games like Half-Life and Portal.
Valve Corp. plays a big role in PC game sales through Steam, a digital platform for buying, selling and playing video games.
Steam reached 1 billion accounts in 2019 and continues to set active user records.
Forbes estimates that Newell owns at least one half of the company, which operates out of Bellevue, Washington.
forbes_facts: Newell was hired by Steve Ballmer as Microsoft's 271st employee after dropping out of Harvard.
Valve released a hand-held gaming console in 2022 called the Steamdeck, which lets gamers play a variety of Steam's offerings on the portable device.

name: Tony Tamer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Tony Tamer is the cofounder and co-executive chairman of H.I.G. Capital, a private equity firm with $70 billion under management.
Tamer launched H.I.G. Capital in 1993 with Sami Mnaymneh; the duo have been masters of middle-market private equity deals.
In addition to operations in Europe and Latin America, H.I.G. also runs a large credit business.
Prior to founding H.I.G. Capital, Tamer was a partner at Bain & Company.
forbes_facts: Tamer fundraised for his former Bain colleague Mitt Romney's 2012 presidential campaign as a co-chair of his Florida finance team.

name: Bajaj siblings
forbes_bio: The three Bajaj siblings are the children and heirs of the late Rahul Bajaj, who was chairman emeritus of the storied Bajaj Group until his death in February 2022.
The group was founded by their great-grandfather Jamnalal Bajaj, who set up the group in 1926 and was a follower of Mahatma Gandhi.
Today, the Bajaj Group is a conglomerate of 40 companies in sectors such as two-wheelers, financial services and electrical appliances.
Rajiv Bajaj, the older brother, runs Bajaj Auto, while his younger brother Sanjiv is in charge of the financial services business. Their sister, Sunaina, is not involved in the business.

name: Chandru Raheja
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: One of four brothers of a property family, Chandru Raheja ventured out on his own in 1996.
Today his privately held K. Raheja Corp. is one of Mumbai's leading developers and is run by his sons Neel and Ravi.
Raheja is known for its IT parks, hotels, malls and department store chain, Shoppers Stop.
His Chalet Hotels, which owns a string of hotels such as the J.W. Marriott in Mumbai and the Westin in Hyderabad, was listed in 2019.
In 2020, Raheja listed part of his commercial properties, co-owned with private equity firm Blackstone, under the Mindspace Business Parks REIT.

name: John Gandel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: John Gandel owns half of the southern hemisphere's largest shopping mall, Chadstone, with more than 500 stores in eastern Melbourne.
He also has a big stake in listed property trust Vicinity Centres, which owns the other half of Chadstone, plus other malls and outlets.
He first got rich by expanding his Polish immigrant parents' clothing chain for women, Sussan, now owned by his niece, Naomi Milgrom.
He made most of his wealth from the shopping malls he bought from Myer department stores for $37 million in the 1980s.
Gandel owns Point Leo Estate in the state of Victoria, which has a 50-acre vineyard and a sculpture park with 60 works.
forbes_facts: Gandel says the key to his success was the deregulation of shopping hours and shopping becoming a leisure activity.
He maintains Gandel Philanthropy, one of Australia's largest charitable funds.
